chapters.title: Jehoahaz, Jehoash and the Death of Elisha
chapters.html:
2 Kings 13

Jehoahaz King of Israel

1In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.

2He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin; he did not turn from them.

3The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, all the days.

4Then Jehoahaz entreated the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for He saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.

5The LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they came out from under the hand of Aram, and the sons of Israel lived in their tents as before.

6Yet they did not turn from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, with which he made Israel to sin; they walked in them. The Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.

7For the king of Aram had left Jehoahaz no army but fifty horsemen, ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, because he had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.

8The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, all that he did and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

9Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Joash his son reigned in his place.

Jehoash King of Israel

10In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.

11He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin; he walked in them.

12The rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

13Joash lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

The Arrow of Victory

14Now Elisha had fallen sick with the sickness of which he would die, and Joash king of Israel came down to him and wept over his face and said, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"

15Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows.

16He said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So he put his hand on it, and Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.

17He said, "Open the window eastward," and he opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" and he shot. He said, "The LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You shall strike the Arameans at Aphek until you have made an end of them."

18He said, "Take the arrows," and he took them. He said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground," and he struck three times and stopped.

19The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck the Arameans until you had made an end of them. But now you will strike the Arameans only three times."

The Bones of Elisha

20Elisha died, and they buried him. Bands of Moabites would come into the land as the year came in.

21And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that they saw a band, and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha. The man went down and touched the bones of Elisha, and he came to life and stood up on his feet.

22Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

23But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them, and He turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and He has not cast them from His presence until now.

24Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.

25Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Ben-hadad had taken in war from the hand of Jehoahaz his father. Three times Joash struck him down, and he recovered the cities of Israel.

Notes

  • v4 "Jehoahaz entreated the LORD" — va-yechal et penei YHWH, he softened the face of the LORD, the words of Moses pleading for the people after the golden calf (Exodus 32:11). A king who keeps Jeroboam's calves (v2) uses Moses' words, and the LORD listens.

  • v5 "The LORD gave Israel a deliverer" — moshia, the word of the judges: the LORD raised up a deliverer (Judges 3:9). The deliverer is not named; the Greek has salvation. The next chapter says the LORD saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash (14:27).

  • v5 "as before" — ki-tmol shilshom, as yesterday and the day before, as in Pharaoh's order about the straw (Exodus 5:7).

  • v14 "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" — Elisha's own cry when Elijah was taken up (2:12), now spoken over Elisha, by a king.

  • v17 "The LORD's arrow of victory" — chets teshu'ah la-YHWH. Teshu'ah is salvation, victory, the noun of moshia in v5. Aphek is where Ahab defeated an earlier Ben-hadad (1 Kings 20:26–30). The Greek lacks Elisha said, Shoot! and he shot.

  • vv18–19, 25 "he struck three times and stopped… Three times Joash struck him down" — the prophet's word kept to the number the king struck.

  • v20 "as the year came in" — ba shanah, a year came, with no article; the Greek has as the year came. When in the year is meant is not said.

  • v21 "touched the bones of Elisha, and he came to life" — Sirach praises Elisha for it: in his sleep his body prophesied… in his death his works were marvelous (Sirach 48:13–14).

  • v23 "He has not cast them from His presence until now" — ad attah, until now, which the Greek lacks. The book records when it happened: until He had cast them out from His presence (17:20).

chapters.title: Amaziah and Jeroboam II
chapters.html:
2 Kings 14

Amaziah King of Judah

1In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah began to reign.

2He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

3He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like David his father. He did according to all that Joash his father had done.

4Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

5And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, that he struck down his servants who had struck down the king his father.

6But he did not put to death the sons of the murderers, according to what is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin."

7He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and took Sela in battle, and called its name Joktheel, as it is to this day.

The Thistle and the Cedar

8Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other."

9Jehoash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "A thistle in Lebanon sent to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as wife.' Then a wild beast in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.

10You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your glory, and stay at home. Why should you provoke trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"

11But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

12Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his tent.

13Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. He came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

14He took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.

15The rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

16Jehoash lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.

The Death of Amaziah

17Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.

18The rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

19They made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.

20They carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.

21All the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

22He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his fathers.

Jeroboam King of Israel

23In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.

24He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

25He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which He spoke by His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.

26For the LORD saw that the affliction of Israel was very bitter: there was none left, bond or free, and there was no helper for Israel.

27The LORD had not said that He would wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens, so He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

28The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, all that he did and his might, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

29Jeroboam lay down with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • v6 "Fathers shall not be put to death for sons" — the law of Deuteronomy 24:16, quoted word for word. It is the only place in Kings where the words of the law are quoted; elsewhere the book says only as it is written (1 Kings 2:3; 2 Kings 23:21).

  • v7 "Sela… Joktheel" — ha-sela, the rock. Amaziah renames a conquered Edomite stronghold, as the Danites renamed Laish (Judges 18:29).

  • vv8, 11 "Come, let us face each other" — nitra'eh fanim, let us look one another in the face: a challenge to battle. Verse 11 uses the same verb for the battle itself.

  • v9 "A thistle in Lebanon sent to a cedar in Lebanon" — a fable in the manner of Jotham's, where the bramble says let fire come out of the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon (Judges 9:15). There the low plant threatens the cedar; here the low plant asks to marry into its house and is trampled. Choach is the thistle or thorn; Jotham's plant is atad.

  • v10 "Enjoy your glory, and stay at home" — hikkaved, be honored, from kavod, glory.

  • v14 "hostages" — benei ha-ta'arubot, sons of pledges, found only here and in the same account in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 25:24).

  • v21 "Azariah" — the king called Uzziah in 15:13, 30, 32, 34 and in Isaiah 6:1. Azaryahu, the LORD has helped; Uzziyyahu, the LORD is my strength.

  • v25 "His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher" — the prophet of the book of Jonah (Jonah 1:1). Here he speaks good news for Israel; there he is sent to Nineveh.

  • v26 "very bitter… none left, bond or free" — the Hebrew has moreh, which elsewhere means rebellious (a stubborn and rebellious son, Deuteronomy 21:18) or teacher; the affliction of Israel was very rebellious does not make sense. The Greek has pikran, bitter, and the text follows the Greek. Efes atsur ve-efes azuv, none left, bond or free, are the words of the Song of Moses: the LORD will judge His people… when He sees that their strength is gone and there is none left, bond or free (Deuteronomy 32:36).

  • v28 "restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel" — le-Yehudah be-Yisra'el, as the Hebrew and the Greek both have it. Neither city is said anywhere else to have belonged to Judah, and the phrase is not explained. The text keeps it as it stands.

chapters.title: Azariah, Jotham and the Last Kings of Israel
chapters.html:
2 Kings 15

Azariah King of Judah

1In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah began to reign.

2He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

3He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

4Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

5The LORD struck the king, and he had blight until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house. Jotham the king's son was over the household, governing the people of the land.

6The rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

7Azariah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David, and Jotham his son reigned in his place.

Zechariah, Shallum and Menahem

8In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.

9He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his fathers had done. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

10Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him and struck him down before the people, and put him to death and reigned in his place.

11The rest of the acts of Zechariah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

12This was the word of the LORD that He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel." So it came to be.

13Shallum son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned one full month in Samaria.

14Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and put him to death and reigned in his place.

15The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy that he made, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

16At that time Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territory from Tirzah, because they did not open to him. So he struck it, and he ripped open all its pregnant women.

17In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi began to reign over Israel, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.

18He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. All his days he did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

19Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, so that his hand might be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.

20Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the men of worth, fifty shekels of silver from each man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.

21The rest of the acts of Menahem and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

22Menahem lay down with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.

Pekahiah and Pekah

23In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.

24He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

25Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house, with Argob and with Arieh; with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. He put him to death and reigned in his place.

26The rest of the acts of Pekahiah and all that he did are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

27In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.

28He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

29In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he carried the people into exile to Assyria.

30Hoshea son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down and put him to death, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

31The rest of the acts of Pekah and all that he did are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Jotham King of Judah

32In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.

33He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.

34He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD; he did according to all that Uzziah his father had done.

35Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.

36The rest of the acts of Jotham and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

37In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

38Jotham lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • v5 "The LORD struck the king, and he had blight… in a separate house" — metsora, from tsara'at, blight. Beit ha-chofshit, the house of freedom, found only here and in Chronicles, which gives the cause: Uzziah went into the house of the LORD to burn incense, and the blight broke out on his forehead before the priests (2 Chronicles 26:19–21). Freedom here is release from duty, the separation the law requires: He shall live alone; his home shall be outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46).

  • v10 "struck him down before the people" — qoval am, with qoval, an Aramaic word for before. The Greek reads it as a place, in Keblaam.

  • v12 "Your sons to the fourth generation… So it came to be" — the word of 10:30 kept: Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam, Zechariah. Zechariah reigns six months.

  • v13 "one full month" — yerach yamim, a month of days. Shallum reigns a month; Zimri reigned seven days (1 Kings 16:15).

  • v16 "Tiphsah… from Tirzah… ripped open all its pregnant women" — Tiphsah is the Euphrates crossing named as the far edge of Solomon's rule (1 Kings 4:24), a long way from Tirzah; the Greek has Tirzah in both places. The text keeps the Hebrew. What Elisha wept to foresee from Hazael, rip open their pregnant women (8:12), an Israelite king does to Israelites.

  • vv19–20 "Pul… Tiglath-pileser" — Chronicles names Pul king of Assyria and Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria together (1 Chronicles 5:26). Men of worth, gibborei ha-chayil, elsewhere fighting men (1 Chronicles 7:2); here the worth is measured in silver, fifty shekels a head.

  • v25 "with Argob and with Arieh" — Argov, ha-aryeh, the lion: two names, or two men killed with the king; the text does not explain them. The Greek has from the four hundred for of the Gileadites.

  • v29 "Galilee, all the land of Naphtali… into exile to Assyria" — the first exile of Israelites that Kings records. Isaiah speaks of this time: in the former time He brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter He will make glorious… Galilee of the nations (Isaiah 9:1), the words Matthew applies to Jesus (Matthew 4:15–16).

  • v30 "in the twentieth year of Jotham" — Jotham reigns sixteen years (v33). The text keeps the number as it stands.

  • v37 "Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah" — the two kings of Isaiah 7, these two smoldering stumps of firebrands (Isaiah 7:4).

chapters.title: Ahaz and the Altar from Damascus
chapters.html:
2 Kings 16

Ahaz King of Judah

1In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.

2Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as David his father had done.

3He walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.

4He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills and under every leafy tree.

Ahaz Calls on Assyria

5Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to wage war. They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.

6At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the men of Judah out of Elath. The Edomites came to Elath and have lived there to this day.

7Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."

8Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and sent it to the king of Assyria as a bribe.

9The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria went up against Damascus and took it, carried its people into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.

The Altar from Damascus

10King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he saw the altar that was at Damascus. King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, in all its workmanship.

11Uriah the priest built the altar; according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so Uriah the priest made it, before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.

12When the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar. The king drew near to the altar and went up on it,

13and he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and dashed the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.

14The bronze altar that was before the LORD he moved from the front of the house, from between his altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of his altar.

15King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their grain offering and their drink offerings. Dash on it all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. The bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by."

16Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded.

17King Ahaz cut off the panels of the stands and removed the basins from them. He took down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a pavement of stone.

18The covered way for the Sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king's outer entrance, he turned away from the house of the LORD because of the king of Assyria.

19The rest of the acts of Ahaz that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

20Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • v3 "made his son pass through the fire, according to the detestable practices of the nations" — to'avot, detestable things. The law names it first among the practices of the nations: There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire (Deuteronomy 18:10). Ahaz is the first king of Judah of whom it is said.

  • vv5–7 "Rezin… and Pekah… I am your servant and your son" — the war of Isaiah 7, when the prophet met Ahaz and told him, Be careful and be quiet; do not fear (Isaiah 7:4). Here Ahaz turns to Assyria instead, calling himself the Assyrian king's servant and son.

  • v6 "recovered Elath for Aram… The Edomites came to Elath" — the Hebrew writes Arameans in the second clause and the scribes read Edomites; the text follows the read form, and so does the Greek. In Hebrew Aram and Edom differ by one letter. Elath had been built and restored to Judah by Azariah (14:22).

  • v8 "as a bribe" — shochad, which the law forbids: You shall not take a bribe (Exodus 23:8). The silver comes out of the house of the LORD.

  • v9 "carried its people into exile to Kir" — as Amos said of Aram: the people of Aram shall go into exile to Kir (Amos 1:5). Amos also names Kir as the place the LORD brought Aram from (Amos 9:7).

  • v10 "the likeness of the altar and its pattern" — tavnit, the word of the dwelling in the wilderness: According to all that I show you — the pattern of the dwelling (Exodus 25:9). The pattern for the LORD's altar now comes from Damascus.

  • vv12–13 "went up on it, and he burned his burnt offering" — the king offers on the new altar himself.

  • v15 "The bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by" — yihyeh li le-vaqqer. Baqqer is to inquire, to examine, as of reading omens from an offering; the Greek reads la-boqer, for the morning. The text keeps the Hebrew; what Ahaz meant to do at the old altar is not said.

  • v18 "The covered way for the Sabbath" — written meisakh, read musakh, found only here; covered is the sense of the root sakhakh, to cover. The Greek has the foundation of the seat. What was done to it, and why because of the king of Assyria, the text does not explain.

speech.text: 2 Kings 16
Ahaz King of Judah
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as David his father had done.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.
He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills and under every leafy tree.
Ahaz Calls on Assyria
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to wage war. They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the men of Judah out of Elath. The Edomites came to Elath and have lived there to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and sent it to the king of Assyria as a bribe.
The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria went up against Damascus and took it, carried its people into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.
The Altar from Damascus

King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he saw the altar that was at Damascus. King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, in all its workmanship.
Uriah the priest built the altar; according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so Uriah the priest made it, before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
When the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar. The king drew near to the altar and went up on it,
and he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and dashed the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
The bronze altar that was before the LORD he moved from the front of the house, from between his altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of his altar.

King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their grain offering and their drink offerings. Dash on it all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. The bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by."
Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cut off the panels of the stands and removed the basins from them. He took down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a pavement of stone.

The rest of the acts of Ahaz that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

chapters.title: The Fall of Samaria
chapters.html:
2 Kings 17

Hoshea, the Last King of Israel

1In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Israel, and he reigned nine years.

2He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.

3Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

4But the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had year by year. So the king of Assyria shut him up and bound him in prison.

5Then the king of Assyria came up through all the land, and he came up to Samaria and besieged it three years.

6In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel into exile to Assyria. He settled them in Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

Why Israel Fell

7This happened because the sons of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They feared other gods

8and walked in the statutes of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel, and in the statutes the kings of Israel had made.

9The sons of Israel did in secret things that were not right against the LORD their God. They built for themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.

10They set up for themselves pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every leafy tree,

11and there they burned incense on all the high places, as the nations did whom the LORD carried away before them. They did evil things to provoke the LORD to anger,

12and they served idols, of which the LORD had said to them, "You shall not do this."

13Yet the LORD warned Israel and Judah by every prophet and every seer, saying, "Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments and My statutes, according to all the law that I commanded your fathers and that I sent to you by My servants the prophets."

14But they would not listen, and they stiffened their necks, like the necks of their fathers, who did not believe in the LORD their God.

15They rejected His statutes and His covenant that He made with their fathers, and His testimonies with which He warned them. They went after emptiness and became empty, and after the nations that were around them, of whom the LORD had commanded them not to do as they did.

16They forsook all the commandments of the LORD their God and made for themselves molten images, two calves. They made an Asherah, bowed down to all the host of heaven and served Baal.

17They made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and read omens, and sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.

18So the LORD was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None was left but the tribe of Judah alone.

19Judah also did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the statutes Israel had made.

20The LORD rejected all the seed of Israel. He afflicted them and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until He had cast them out from His presence.

21For He tore Israel from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and made them sin a great sin.

22The sons of Israel walked in all the sins that Jeroboam did; they did not turn from them,

23until the LORD removed Israel from His presence, as He had spoken by all His servants the prophets. So Israel was carried into exile from its own land to Assyria, to this day.

The Settlers in Samaria

24The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.

25And it came to pass, at the beginning of their living there, that they did not fear the LORD. So the LORD sent lions among them, which kept killing some of them.

26So they said to the king of Assyria, "The nations that you carried away and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the rule of the god of the land. He has sent lions among them, and they are killing them, because they do not know the rule of the god of the land."

27Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, "Take there one of the priests whom you carried away from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the rule of the god of the land."

28So one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and he taught them how they should fear the LORD.

29But every nation went on making gods of its own and put them in the houses of the high places that the Samarians had made, every nation in the cities in which they lived.

30The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, the men of Hamath made Ashima,

31and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak. The Sepharvites burned their sons in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

32They also feared the LORD, and they appointed from among all their people priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.

33They feared the LORD and served their own gods, according to the rule of the nations from which they had been carried away.

34To this day they do according to their former rules. They do not fear the LORD, and they do not do according to their statutes or their rules, or according to the law and the commandment that the LORD commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He named Israel.

35The LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other gods or bow down to them or serve them or sacrifice to them,

36but the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm, Him you shall fear, to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.

37The statutes and the rules, the law and the commandment that He wrote for you, you shall be careful to do all the days. You shall not fear other gods,

38and the covenant that I have made with you, you shall not forget. You shall not fear other gods,

39but the LORD your God you shall fear, and He will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."

40But they would not listen, and they do according to their former rule.

41So these nations feared the LORD and served their carved images; their sons and their sons' sons also, as their fathers did, so they do to this day.

Notes

  • v4 "So king of Egypt" — So is named nowhere else; the Greek has Segor.

  • v6 "carried Israel into exile to Assyria" — Samaria falls in the ninth year of Hoshea (18:9–11). Moses had warned it: the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples (Deuteronomy 28:64).

  • v9 "did in secret things that were not right" — va-yechappe'u, found only here. In secret is the sense the context gives; it matches chafah, to cover, a verb that differs by its last letter, as David went up with his head covered (2 Samuel 15:30). The Greek has they clothed themselves with words.

  • v15 "went after emptiness and became empty" — va-yelkhu acharei ha-hevel va-yehbalu, word for word in Jeremiah: they went after emptiness and became empty (Jeremiah 2:5). Hevel is breath, vapor, the word of Ecclesiastes and the name Abel; people become what they follow.

  • v17 "sold themselves to do evil" — va-yitmakkeru, said earlier in Kings only of Ahab (1 Kings 21:20, 25). Moses used the same verb for the end of the curses: there you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies (Deuteronomy 28:68).

  • v20 "until He had cast them out from His presence" — the end of what 13:23 said had not happened until now.

  • v21 "He tore Israel from the house of David" — qara Yisra'el, with no subject; the words can also be read Israel tore away from the house of David. The verb is the LORD's in Ahijah's sign: I am about to tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon (1 Kings 11:31), and the text reads it so. Written va-yada, read va-yaddach, drove away.

  • vv26–40 "the rule of the god of the land… their former rules" — mishpat, one word throughout: the settlers do not know the rule of the god of the land (vv26–27) and follow the rule of the nations (v33), while the LORD's statutes and rules (vv34, 37) are what Israel was given. The god of the land is the LORD, and the priest teaches them how they should fear the LORD (v28).

  • v31 "burned their sons in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech" — written Sepharim, read Sepharvaim, as in v24.

  • vv32–33, 41 "They feared the LORD and served their own gods" — and then v34, they do not fear the LORD: fear of the LORD alongside other gods is counted as not fearing Him at all, as the commands of vv35–39 say three times, You shall not fear other gods.

chapters.title: Hezekiah and the Rabshakeh
chapters.html:
2 Kings 18

Hezekiah King of Judah

1And it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.

2He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi daughter of Zechariah.

3He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that David his father had done.

4He removed the high places, broke the pillars and cut down the Asherah. He broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it; it was called Nehushtan.

5He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel, so that after him there was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him.

6He held fast to the LORD; he did not turn from following Him, but kept His commandments that the LORD commanded Moses.

7The LORD was with him; wherever he went out, he prospered. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.

8He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.

Samaria Taken

9And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.

10At the end of three years they took it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.

11The king of Assyria carried Israel into exile to Assyria and put them in Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,

12because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God but transgressed His covenant, all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded; they would neither listen nor do it.

Sennacherib Comes Up

13In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.

14Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, "I have done wrong; withdraw from me. Whatever you put on me I will bear." The king of Assyria laid on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

15Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house.

16At that time Hezekiah stripped the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave the gold to the king of Assyria.

17The king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rab-saris and the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem, and when they arrived, they stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Washer's Field.

18When they called for the king, Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebnah the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came out to them.

The Rabshakeh's Speech

19The Rabshakeh said to them, "Say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?

20You say — but it is only a word of the lips — that you have counsel and strength for war. Now, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?

21Now you are trusting in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it and go into it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

22But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem, "You shall bow down before this altar in Jerusalem"?'

23So now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them.

24How then can you turn back a single governor among the least of my master's servants, when you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

25Now, have I come up against this place to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

26Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebnah and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."

27But the Rabshakeh said to them, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?"

28Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah, and he spoke and said, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!

29Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you out of his hand.

30Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

31Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each will drink the water of his own cistern,

32until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, so that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you, saying, "The LORD will deliver us."

33Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

34Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

35Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their lands out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'"

36But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."

37Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

Notes

  • vv13–37 and Isaiah 36 — the same account stands in Isaiah 36–39, nearly word for word. Isaiah lacks vv14–16, the tribute, and in v17 sends only the Rabshakeh.

  • v4 "the bronze serpent that Moses had made… it was called Nehushtan" — nechash ha-nechoshet, the serpent of bronze, from the wilderness: Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on the pole (Numbers 21:9). Nechushtan joins the two words, nachash, serpent, and nechoshet, bronze. What the LORD gave for healing had become something burned incense to.

  • vv5, 19–24, 30 "He trusted in the LORD… What is this confidence in which you trust?" — batach, to trust, said of Hezekiah in v5 and then used by the Rabshakeh eight times (vv19 twice, 20, 21 twice, 22, 24, 30): the whole speech is an attack on that one word.

  • v5 "after him there was none like him" — the same is said of Josiah: before him there was no king like him… and after him none arose like him (23:25). Hezekiah is unmatched in trust, Josiah in turning to the LORD with all his heart.

  • v17 "the Tartan, the Rab-saris and the Rabshakeh" — titles, not names. Rav-shaqeh is chief cupbearer in its Hebrew sound, from shaqah, to give drink; rav-saris, chief official. The text keeps the received forms.

  • v21 "the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt" — the same picture in Ezekiel: Egypt has been a staff of reed to the house of Israel; when they took hold of you by the hand, you splintered (Ezekiel 29:6–7).

  • v23 "make a wager with my master" — hit'arev, from arav, to pledge, the root of the sons of pledges, the hostages Jehoash took from Jerusalem (14:14).

  • v27 "to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine" — the text follows the read forms, tso'atam and mei ragleihem, the water of their feet; the written forms are coarser words for the same things. The meaning is the same either way.

  • vv31–32 "each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree… a land of olive oil and honey" — the Rabshakeh offers the peace of Solomon's days, each man under his vine and under his fig tree (1 Kings 4:25), and a land described as the LORD described Canaan, a land of olive oil and honey (Deuteronomy 8:8), only it lies in exile. Make peace with me is asu itti verakhah, make a blessing with me.

  • v34 "Hena and Ivvah" — Isaiah 36:19 and the Greek here lack these two names.

At that time Hezekiah stripped the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave the gold to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rab-saris and the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem, and when they arrived, they stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Washer's Field.
When they called for the king, Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebnah the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came out to them.
The Rabshakeh's Speech
The Rabshakeh said to them, "Say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?
You say — but it is only a word of the lips — that you have counsel and strength for war. Now, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Now you are trusting in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it and go into it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem, "You shall bow down before this altar in Jerusalem"?'
So now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them.
How then can you turn back a single governor among the least of my master's servants, when you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Now, have I come up against this place to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebnah and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."

But the Rabshakeh said to them, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?"
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah, and he spoke and said, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you out of his hand.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each will drink the water of his own cistern,

until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, so that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you, saying, "The LORD will deliver us."
Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their lands out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'"
But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

chapters.title: Isaiah's Word and the Deliverance of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Kings 19

Hezekiah Sends to Isaiah

1And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.

2He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.

3They said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: 'This day is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. The children have come to the mouth of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth.

4It may be that the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.'"

5So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,

6and Isaiah said to them, "Say this to your master: 'Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled Me.

7I will put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and return to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"

Sennacherib's Letter

8The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.

9Then the king heard it said of Tirhakah king of Cush, "He has come out to fight against you." So he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,

10"Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

11You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. Will you be delivered?

12Did the gods of the nations deliver them, the nations my fathers destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?

13Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?'"

Hezekiah's Prayer

14Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.

15Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, "O LORD, the God of Israel, who is enthroned on the cherubim, You are God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made the heavens and the earth.

16Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.

17Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,

18and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were no gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone; so they destroyed them.

19So now, O LORD our God, save us, please, from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You, O LORD, are God alone."

The Word of the LORD against Sennacherib

20Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: What you have prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.

21"This is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him:
She despises you, she scorns you,
the virgin daughter of Zion;
behind you she shakes her head,
the daughter of Jerusalem.

22Whom have you defied and reviled?
Against whom have you raised your voice
and lifted your eyes on high?
Against the Holy One of Israel!

23By your messengers you have defied the Lord,
and you have said, 'With the multitude of my chariots
I have gone up to the heights of the mountains,
to the far reaches of Lebanon.
I cut down its tallest cedars,
its choicest cypresses;
I entered its farthest lodging place,
its densest forest.

24I dug wells and drank foreign waters,
and with the sole of my feet I dried up
all the streams of Egypt.'

25Have you not heard?
Long ago I made it;
from days of old I formed it;
now I have brought it to pass,
that you should turn fortified cities
into heaps of ruins,

26while their inhabitants, short of strength,
were dismayed and put to shame.
They were like the grass of the field
and the green herb,
like grass on the housetops,
scorched before it is grown.

27I know your sitting down,
your going out and your coming in,
and your raging against Me.

28Because you have raged against Me
and your arrogance has come up to My ears,
I will put My hook in your nose
and My bit in your lips,
and I will turn you back on the way
by which you came.

29"This shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; then in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

30The survivors of the house of Judah who remain shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

31For out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

32"Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city or shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with a shield, nor cast up a siege mound against it.

33By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, declares the LORD.

34For I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant."

The Night of the Messenger

35And it came to pass that night that the messenger of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When people rose early in the morning, they were all dead bodies.

36So Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went home, and lived in Nineveh.

37And it came to pass, as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • v3 "The children have come to the mouth of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth" — mashber, the breaking, the opening of the womb at birth; Hosea uses it of Ephraim, an unwise son who does not stand in place at the breaking forth of children (Hosea 13:13). A birth that cannot be completed is Hezekiah's picture of the city.

  • vv4, 16 "to defy the living God" — lecharef Elohim chai, the words of David at the valley of Elah: who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God? (1 Samuel 17:26).

  • v7 "I will put a spirit in him" — ruach, lowercase: not the Spirit of the LORD but a disposition given to the king, as the evil spirit sent on Saul (1 Samuel 16:14).

  • v15 "who is enthroned on the cherubim" — yoshev ha-keruvim, the title of the LORD over the ark (1 Samuel 4:4).

  • v23 "With the multitude of my chariots" — written be-rekhev, with chariotry, read be-rov rikhbi; the text follows the read form.

  • v24 "foreign waters… the streams of Egypt" — ye'orei matsor, with Matsor, a poetic name for Egypt, as in the streams of Egypt will dry up (Isaiah 19:6). The Greek reads it as matsor, siege. Isaiah's copy of this poem lacks foreign (Isaiah 37:25).

  • v26 "scorched before it is grown" — shedefah, blighted, as the thin ears scorched by the east wind in Pharaoh's dream (Genesis 41:6). Isaiah's copy has shedemah, a field (Isaiah 37:27).

  • v29 "what grows of itself… what springs from that" — safiach, the self-sown grain of the sabbath year, which the law forbids to be reaped (Leviticus 25:5); sachish is found only here, and Isaiah's copy spells it shachis. Two years without sowing, the third year a harvest.

  • v31 "The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" — the same words close Isaiah's promise of the child on David's throne (Isaiah 9:7).

  • v37 "Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons… the land of Ararat" — Adrammelech is also the name of the god of 17:31. Ararat, where the ark came to rest (Genesis 8:4). The king who asked where are the gods of the nations? (18:34) dies in the house of his own god.

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Illness and the Envoys from Babylon
chapters.html:
2 Kings 20

Fifteen Years Added

1In those days Hezekiah became sick and was near death. Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz came to him and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Set your house in order, for you shall die; you shall not live.'"

2Then he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying,

3"Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." Hezekiah wept bitterly.

4And it came to pass, before Isaiah had gone out of the middle court, that the word of the LORD came to him, saying,

5"Turn back and say to Hezekiah the leader of My people, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.

6I will add fifteen years to your days. I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"

7Isaiah said, "Take a cake of figs." They took it and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.

The Shadow on the Steps

8Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What is the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"

9Isaiah said, "This is the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do what He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?"

10Hezekiah answered, "It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. Rather, let the shadow go back ten steps."

11Isaiah the prophet called to the LORD, and He brought the shadow back ten steps, by which it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz.

The Envoys from Babylon

12At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

13Hezekiah was glad of them, and he showed them all his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his armory and all that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.

14Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say? From where did they come to you?" Hezekiah said, "They have come from a far country, from Babylon."

15He said, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them."

16Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:

17The days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be carried to Babylon. Nothing shall be left, says the LORD.

18Some of your sons, who will come from you, whom you will father, shall be taken away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."

19Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he said, "Is it not so, if there will be peace and security in my days?"

20The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

21Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–11 and Isaiah 38 — Isaiah tells the same story and adds the song Hezekiah wrote after he recovered (Isaiah 38:9–20); there the fig cake comes at the end (Isaiah 38:21).

  • v3 "in faithfulness and with a whole heart" — be-emet u-ve-levav shalem, the whole heart the narrator found lacking in Solomon: his heart was not whole with the LORD his God (1 Kings 11:4).

  • v4 "the middle court" — the read form chatser, court; the written form is ha-ir, the city. The Greek has the middle court.

  • v5 "the leader of My people… the God of David your father" — nagid, the title the LORD gave Saul and David (1 Samuel 9:16; 13:14). Isaiah's copy lacks the leader of My people, I will heal you and On the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.

  • v7 "a cake of figs… on the boil" — shechin, the word of the boils of Egypt (Exodus 9:9) and of the boil the priest inspects (Leviticus 13:18).

  • vv9–11 "ten steps… the steps of Ahaz" — ma'alot, steps, the word of the stairway. The steps of Ahaz are named nowhere else. Ma'alot is also the word of the Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134).

  • v12 "Berodach-baladan son of Baladan" — Isaiah's copy and the Greek spell the name Merodach; b and m are both made with the lips.

  • v13 "Hezekiah was glad of them" — the Hebrew has va-yishma, he listened to them; Isaiah's copy has va-yismach, he was glad, and so does the Greek. The two words differ by one letter, and the scene, the king showing all his treasure, bears out glad. The text follows Isaiah and the Greek.

  • v18 "they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon" — Daniel opens with it: Nebuchadnezzar orders the chief of his eunuchs to bring some of the sons of Israel, of the royal seed (Daniel 1:3). Written yiqqach, read yiqqachu, they shall be taken.

  • v19 "Is it not so, if there will be peace and security in my days?" — shalom ve-emet. The same emet Hezekiah claimed in his prayer (v3), now as security for his own lifetime.

chapters.title: Manasseh and Amon
chapters.html:
2 Kings 21

Manasseh King of Judah

1Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.

2He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.

3He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed. He set up altars for Baal and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel had done, and he bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.

4He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will put My name."

5He built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

6He made his son pass through the fire, practiced soothsaying and read omens, and appointed those who deal with ghosts and spirits. He did much evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

7He set the carved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which the LORD had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.

8I will not again make the feet of Israel wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they will be careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the instruction that My servant Moses commanded them."

9But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the sons of Israel.

The Word against Jerusalem

10The LORD spoke by His servants the prophets, saying,

11"Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these detestable things, doing more evil than all that the Amorites did who were before him, and has made Judah also to sin with his idols,

12therefore thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I am about to bring such evil on Jerusalem and Judah that both ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.

13I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.

14I will cast off the remnant of My inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies, and they shall become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,

15because they have done what is evil in My eyes and have provoked Me to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day."

16Moreover, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to the other, besides his sin with which he made Judah to sin, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

17The rest of the acts of Manasseh, all that he did and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

18Manasseh lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and Amon his son reigned in his place.

Amon King of Judah

19Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

20He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done.

21He walked in all the way in which his father walked, served the idols that his father served and bowed down to them.

22He forsook the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.

23The servants of Amon conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.

24But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

25The rest of the acts of Amon that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

  • v3 "as Ahab king of Israel had done" — the king of Judah is measured against the worst king of Israel, and in v13 Jerusalem against Samaria and the house of Ahab.

  • v6 "practiced soothsaying and read omens… ghosts and spirits" — the same list the law forbids: one who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, a soothsayer, one who reads omens… one who asks a ghost or a spirit (Deuteronomy 18:10–11). Manasseh does five of its nine.

chapters.title: The Book Found in the House of the LORD
chapters.html:
2 Kings 22

Josiah King of Judah

1Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.

2He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in all the way of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

The Book of the Instruction

3And it came to pass in the eighteenth year of King Josiah that the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the secretary, to the house of the LORD, saying,

4"Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and let him total the money that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people.

5Let them give it into the hands of those who do the work, who are appointed over the house of the LORD, and let them give it to the workers in the house of the LORD to repair the breaches of the house,

6to the carpenters, the builders and the masons, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the house.

7But no accounting shall be asked from them for the money given into their hands, for they deal faithfully."

8Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

9Then Shaphan the secretary came to the king and brought back word to the king, saying, "Your servants have poured out the money that was found in the house and have given it into the hands of those who do the work, who are appointed over the house of the LORD."

10Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." Shaphan read it before the king.

11And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the book of the instruction, that he tore his clothes.

12The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,

13"Go, inquire of the LORD for me, for the people and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us."

Huldah the Prophetess

14So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke with her.

15She said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,

16Thus says the LORD: I am about to bring evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read.

17Because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, to provoke Me to anger with all the work of their hands, My wrath will be kindled against this place, and it will not be quenched.'

18But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, say this to him: 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: As for the words that you have heard,

19because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before Me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.

20Therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evil that I will bring on this place.'" They brought back word to the king.

Notes

  • v2 "he did not turn aside to the right or to the left" — the law of the king: so that he does not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left (Deuteronomy 17:20). Kings says it of no other king.

  • v4 "let him total the money… the keepers of the threshold" — ve-yattem, let him complete, count out in full. The arrangement of Jehoash's chest (12:9–15), down to the same words in v7: for they deal faithfully (12:15).

  • vv8, 11 "the book of the instruction" — sefer ha-torah, the name Deuteronomy gives itself: Take this book of the instruction and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and let it be there as a witness against you (Deuteronomy 31:26). Found in the house of the LORD, it becomes that witness.

  • v9 "have poured out the money" — hittikhu, poured out, the verb used of metal melted down, as in you shall be melted in the middle of it (Ezekiel 22:21–22).

  • v11 "he tore his clothes" — Josiah's grandfather Hezekiah tore his clothes at the Rabshakeh's words (19:1); Josiah tears his at the words of the book.

  • v14 "Huldah the prophetess… in the Second Quarter" — ha-nevi'ah, as Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Deborah (Judges 4:4) are called. Ba-mishneh, in the second, the newer quarter of the city named by Zephaniah: a wailing from the Second Quarter (Zephaniah 1:10).

  • v19 "because your heart was tender… a desolation and a curse" — rakh levavkha, your heart was soft. Le-shammah ve-liqlalah, the words Jeremiah uses of the land of Judah after its fall (Jeremiah 44:22).

  • v20 "you shall be gathered to your grave in peace" — Josiah dies by the sword of Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo (23:29). In peace is measured by the next words: your eyes shall not see all the evil that comes on Jerusalem.
