chapters.title: Josiah's Covenant and Reform
chapters.html:
2 Kings 23

The Covenant Renewed

1Then the king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

2The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets and all the people, both small and great. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

3The king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments, His testimonies and His statutes with all the heart and all the soul, to establish the words of this covenant that were written in this book. All the people took their stand in the covenant.

The Purge of Judah

4The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second order and the keepers of the threshold to bring out of the temple of the LORD all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.

5He put down the idol priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and the moon, to the constellations and to all the host of heaven.

6He brought out the Asherah from the house of the LORD, outside Jerusalem, to the Brook Kidron, and burned it at the Brook Kidron and ground it to dust, and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.

7He broke down the houses of the consecrated men that were in the house of the LORD, where the women wove hangings for Asherah.

8He brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He broke down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, on the left as one enters the city gate.

9However, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.

10He defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, so that no one might make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

11He did away with the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entrance to the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the official, which was in the precincts, and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

12The altars on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king broke down. He smashed them there and threw their dust into the Brook Kidron.

13The high places that were east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the loathsome thing of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the loathsome thing of Moab and for Milcom the detestable thing of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.

14He broke the pillars in pieces, cut down the Asherim and filled their places with human bones.

Bethel and Samaria

15Moreover, the altar at Bethel, the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, that altar and the high place he broke down. He burned the high place and ground it to dust, and he burned the Asherah.

16As Josiah turned, he saw the graves there on the mountain. He sent and took the bones out of the graves and burned them on the altar and defiled it, according to the word of the LORD that the man of God proclaimed when Jeroboam stood by the altar at the feast. Then Josiah turned and lifted his eyes to the grave of the man of God who had proclaimed these things.

17He said, "What is that marker I see?" The men of the city told him, "It is the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel."

18He said, "Let him be; let no one disturb his bones." So they left his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.

19Josiah also removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made, provoking the LORD to anger. He did to them according to all that he had done at Bethel.

20He sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there on the altars, and burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

The Passover

21The king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this book of the covenant."

22For no such Passover had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, or in all the days of the kings of Israel or of the kings of Judah.

23But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.

24Moreover, Josiah put away the ghosts and the spirits, the household gods, the idols and all the loathsome things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, to establish the words of the instruction that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.

25Before him there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the instruction of Moses, and after him none arose like him.

26Yet the LORD did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, by which His anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.

27The LORD said, "I will remove Judah also from My presence, as I have removed Israel, and I will reject this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"

The Death of Josiah

28The rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

29In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.

30His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him and made him king in place of his father.

Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim

31Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

32He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

33Pharaoh Neco put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he might not reign in Jerusalem, and he laid on the land a fine of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

34Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away, and he came to Egypt and died there.

35Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he taxed the land to give the money at Pharaoh's command. He exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, from each according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neco.

36Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.

37He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

Notes

  • vv2, 21 "the book of the covenant" — sefer ha-berit, the name of the book Moses read at Sinai: He took the book of the covenant and read it in the ears of the people (Exodus 24:7). Josiah reads in their hearing, the same words.

  • v5 "the idol priests… the constellations" — ha-kemarim, a word used only of priests of other gods, as in Zephaniah's the name of the idol priests with the priests (Zephaniah 1:4). Mazzalot, found only here; the Greek leaves it untranslated.

  • v7 "where the women wove hangings for Asherah" — battim, houses; what the women wove is not explained, and the Greek leaves the word untranslated. Ha-qedeshim, the consecrated men, from qadosh, holy.

  • v10 "Topheth… pass through the fire to Molech" — what the law forbids: You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech (Leviticus 18:21). Jeremiah names the place: the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom (Jeremiah 7:31). Written benei Hinnom, sons of Hinnom; read ben Hinnom.

  • v13 "the Mount of Destruction… the loathsome thing… the detestable thing" — har ha-mashchit, the mountain of the destroyer, from shachat, to destroy: the mountain east of Jerusalem where Solomon built the shrines (1 Kings 11:7). Shiqquts and to'evah, the loathsome thing and the detestable thing.

  • vv15–18 "according to the word of the LORD that the man of God proclaimed" — the word spoken to Jeroboam at the altar: A son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name… human bones shall be burned on you (1 Kings 13:2). The old prophet's request is kept too: lay my bones beside his bones (1 Kings 13:31). He is called the prophet who came from Samaria, though he lived in Bethel (1 Kings 13:11); Samaria here is the name of the northern land.

  • v16 "when Jeroboam stood by the altar at the feast. Then Josiah turned and lifted his eyes to the grave" — the Hebrew lacks these words and reads that the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these things: the eye of a copyist slipped from the first the man of God… proclaimed to the second. The Greek keeps the lost words, and v17, What is that marker I see?, needs them. The text follows the Greek.

  • v25 "with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength" — u-vekhol me'odo. The three are joined only here and in the commandment: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength (Deuteronomy 6:5). Josiah is the one king who keeps it word for word.

  • v29 "went up to the king of Assyria… killed him at Megiddo" — al, to or against; the Hebrew does not say which. Chronicles tells it at length: Neco warned Josiah, archers shot him, and he died in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 35:22–24).

  • vv31–34 "Jehoahaz… came to Egypt and died there" — Jeremiah calls him Shallum: Weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he shall return no more (Jeremiah 22:10–11). Written bimlokh, read mimmelokh, so that he might not reign. Written Zebidah, read Zebudah (v36).

But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.

Moreover, Josiah put away the ghosts and the spirits, the household gods, the idols and all the loathsome things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, to establish the words of the instruction that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.

Before him there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the instruction of Moses, and after him none arose like him.
Yet the LORD did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, by which His anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.

The LORD said, "I will remove Judah also from My presence, as I have removed Israel, and I will reject this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
The Death of Josiah
The rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.

His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Neco put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he might not reign in Jerusalem, and he laid on the land a fine of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away, and he came to Egypt and died there.

Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he taxed the land to give the money at Pharaoh's command. He exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, from each according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

chapters.title: Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin and the First Exile
chapters.html:
2 Kings 24

Jehoiakim and the Raiders

1In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

2The LORD sent against him bands of Chaldeans, bands of Arameans, bands of Moabites and bands of Ammonites, and He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by His servants the prophets.

3Surely at the command of the LORD this came upon Judah, to remove them from His presence for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,

4and also for the innocent blood that he shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to pardon.

5The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

6Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

7The king of Egypt did not come out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.

Jehoiachin and the First Exile

8Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.

9He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.

10At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

11Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it,

12and Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother, his servants, his officials and his eunuchs. The king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

13He carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had spoken.

14He carried into exile all Jerusalem, all the officials and all the men of worth, ten thousand exiles, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land.

15He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon, and the king's mother, the king's wives, his eunuchs and the leading men of the land he led into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

16All the men of valor, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand, all of them strong and fit for war, the king of Babylon brought into exile to Babylon.

Zedekiah

17The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.

18Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

19He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

20For because of the anger of the LORD it came to this in Jerusalem and Judah, until He cast them out from His presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

Notes

  • v2 "according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by His servants the prophets" — the word of 21:10–14, spoken in Manasseh's days: I will… give them into the hand of their enemies.

  • vv3–4 "at the command of the LORD… the LORD was not willing to pardon" — al pi YHWH, at the mouth of the LORD; the Greek reads because of the anger of the LORD, as v20 has it in the Hebrew. Josiah's turning did not cancel the sentence on Manasseh's sins (23:26).

  • v7 "from the Brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates" — the borders promised to Abram, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates (Genesis 15:18), now held by Babylon.

  • v8 "Jehoiachin" — called Coniah by Jeremiah: though Coniah… were the signet ring on My right hand, yet I would tear you off (Jeremiah 22:24). Matthew lists him as Jeconiah in the line of Jesus, at the time of the deportation to Babylon (Matthew 1:11–12).

  • v12 "Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon" — yatsa al, went out to, the words of surrender, as the men of Jabesh said, Tomorrow we will come out to you (1 Samuel 11:10). Jehoiachin gives himself up, and the city is not destroyed this time.

  • v13 "cut in pieces all the vessels of gold… as the LORD had spoken" — the word Isaiah gave Hezekiah: all that is in your house… shall be carried to Babylon (20:17).

  • vv14–16 "ten thousand exiles… seven thousand… a thousand" — the numbers given in v14 and in v16 are two counts of the same exile. Jeremiah gives a third: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three (Jeremiah 52:28). Written asarah, read aseret; written ulei, read eilei, the leading men (v15).

  • v14 "the men of worth… the poorest people of the land" — gibborei ha-chayil, the men Menahem taxed fifty shekels a head (15:20). Those left behind are dallat am ha-arets, the poor of the people of the land.

  • v17 "Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle" — dodo, his father's brother: Josiah's son, the third, Zedekiah in Chronicles' list (1 Chronicles 3:15). Babylon renames him as Egypt renamed Eliakim (23:34). Written Chamital, read Chamutal (v18).

  • v20 "because of the anger of the LORD it came to this" — ki al af YHWH, the reading the Greek gives in v3 as well.

chapters.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Kings 25

The Siege and the Breach

1And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. He encamped against it, and they built a siege wall all around it.

2So the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

3In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

4Then the city was breached, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city. The king went by the way of the Arabah.

5But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.

6They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they passed sentence on him.

7They slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, then put out the eyes of Zedekiah, bound him in bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.

The Burning of the House of the LORD

8In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the chief of the slaughterers, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

9He burned the house of the LORD, the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.

10All the army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the slaughterers broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

11The rest of the people who were left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers carried into exile.

12But the chief of the slaughterers left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.

13The pillars of bronze that were in the house of the LORD, the stands and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried the bronze to Babylon.

14They took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes and all the vessels of bronze used in the service.

15The firepans and the basins, what was of gold, in gold, and what was of silver, in silver, the chief of the slaughterers took.

16The two pillars, the one Sea and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD — the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.

17The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and on it was a capital of bronze. The height of the capital was three cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze; and the second pillar had the same, with the network.

18The chief of the slaughterers took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

19From the city he took one official who was set over the men of war, and five men of those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.

20Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

21The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried into exile from its land.

Gedaliah

22Over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

23When all the commanders of the forces and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

24Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."

25And it came to pass in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came with ten men, and they struck down Gedaliah, and he died, along with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

26Then all the people, both small and great, and the commanders of the forces arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

Jehoiachin Released

27And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, lifted the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison.

28He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

29So Jehoiachin put off his prison garments, and he ate bread before the king continually all the days of his life.

30For his allowance, a continual allowance was given him by the king, a portion each day, all the days of his life.

Notes

  • vv1–21 and Jeremiah 52 — the same account closes the book of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 52:4–27, 31–34), and Jeremiah 39 tells it again in part.

  • v3 "In the fourth month, on the ninth day" — the Hebrew has only on the ninth of the month, with no month named. Jeremiah gives it twice, in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month (Jeremiah 52:6; 39:2). The text follows Jeremiah.

  • v4 "all the men of war fled by night" — the Hebrew has no verb: all the men of war by night. Jeremiah has fled and went out of the city by night (Jeremiah 52:7), and the Greek went out by night. The text follows them.

  • v7 "put out the eyes of Zedekiah… brought him to Babylon" — Ezekiel had said of the prince: I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and there he shall die (Ezekiel 12:13).

  • v8 "Nebuzaradan, the chief of the slaughterers" — rav tabbachim, the title of Potiphar, chief of the slaughterers (Genesis 37:36). On the seventh day: Jeremiah has the tenth day (Jeremiah 52:12). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv13–17 "The pillars of bronze… The height of the capital was three cubits" — Solomon's pillars, Jachin and Boaz (1 Kings 7:21). Their capitals were five cubits high (1 Kings 7:16), and Jeremiah also has five (Jeremiah 52:22). The Hebrew here and the Greek both have three; the text keeps them.

  • v19 "five men of those who saw the king's face" — Jeremiah has seven (Jeremiah 52:25). Saw the king's face: those with access to the king.

  • v21 "So Judah was carried into exile from its land" — the same words as the end of Israel: Israel was carried into exile from its own land (17:23).

  • v26 "went to Egypt" — the people return to the land of the exodus, as the curses had said: The LORD will bring you back to Egypt (Deuteronomy 28:68).

  • vv27–30 "lifted the head of Jehoiachin… ate bread before the king continually" — nasa et rosh, the words of Joseph's prison: Pharaoh will lift your head and restore you to your place (Genesis 40:13). The book ends with the king of David's line eating at a foreign king's table, as Mephibosheth always ate at the king's table (2 Samuel 9:13). Jeremiah dates the release on the twenty-fifth day (Jeremiah 52:31).
